subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: After the registration-mode guard is fixed, should OpenClaw accept the `@microsoft/mxc-sdk`/`node-pty` native dependency graph and the upstream argv-carried `--config-base64` sandbox config boundary for this prerelease Windows sandbox plugin?
rationale: This is a first-party sandbox security boundary involving native executables, a build-script dependency, and process-argv visibility of sandbox policy; automation can identify the boundary but cannot decide OpenClaw's acceptance threshold.

options.title: Accept after guard
options.body: Fix the non-full registration side effect first, then have a maintainer/secops owner approve the exact-head dependency graph and documented MXC SDK argv transport before merge.

options.title: Pause for upstream transport
options.body: Keep the PR open but defer merge until MXC SDK provides a non-argv config transport or a stronger policy secrecy story.

options.title: Decline first-party package
options.body: Close or redirect the backend outside first-party OpenClaw packaging if maintainers do not want to own this sandbox dependency boundary.

recommendation.title: Accept after guard
recommendation.body: Fix the non-full registration side effect first, then have a maintainer/secops owner approve the exact-head dependency graph and documented MXC SDK argv transport before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They made the latest item-specific parity and security-acceptance request on this PR.
